title: REALMBREAK
tagline: A WebXR mixed-reality fight for Meta Quest: a villain lands on your real floor, your room shatters into an arena, and the beams clash. Plays in the browser, with a desktop and phone fallback.
stateNote: Per its README it has not yet been tested on a physical headset. It was checked with unit tests, a headless-browser desktop fallback and Meta's WebXR emulator. This page is written from the README and the public site, not from a headset run for this site.
problem: Mixed-reality demos usually need an app store install and a lot of floor space explained in a menu. REALMBREAK runs from a link in the Quest Browser: it finds your floor, a villain teleports onto it, you charge a blast with your bare hands, the room cracks open into a sunlit arena, and you win or lose a beam clash.
audience: Meta Quest 3 and Pro owners who want to try a browser-based mixed-reality game, and anyone curious about WebXR. Desktop and phone visitors get the same scenes in regular 3D.
contribution: It is my project. Vite, TypeScript and Three.js, with no backend. The README says every character, model, texture and sound is generated at runtime, and the repository is MIT licensed.
worksToday: A hosted build at mr.mauricegarcia.com with an Enter AR on Quest button and a Play on this screen fallback.
The README describes four scenes: the villain arrives on your floor, you charge a blast, the room cracks and shatters into an arena, and the beams clash.
Hand tracking, controllers and mouse or touch are all supported inputs, with an auto-fire assist and gaze-dwell Replay so the game does not soft-lock.
limitations: The README says it is not yet tested on a physical headset; hand-gesture and plane-detection behaviour is covered only by unit tests.
The automated XR smoke test is not part of CI and its final Replay step does not pass yet, per the README.
Floor lock needs the headset to have seen the floor; otherwise it falls back to the reference-space floor.
